headline: A nonprofit calls OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens an unacceptable risk, and OpenAI disputes its testing.
score_reason: Pool 7; the claim is attributed to the watchdog and OpenAI's rebuttal is printed, so no lowering; status DISPUTED.
importance_line: Parents and teenagers who use the feature may rely on crisis alerts that the watchdog says often fail, and the doubt is that OpenAI says much of the testing may have taken place before its parental controls were fully active.
summary: The Verge reports that Common Sense Media, a nonprofit that reviews apps for youth safety, says ChatGPT for Teens does not send parents alerts when it should and still does kids' homework. OpenAI answers that the tests may have run before its parental controls were fully active, and Common Sense replies that some accounts were linked long enough and still got no alerts.
notes: Full text read on The Verge (its own reporting with statements from OpenAI and Common Sense). Pool link (WSJ, HTTP 401) names the same assessment; not used as source. Score kept at 7: the claim is attributed and the dispute is printed.
